latestArticle.headline: Braves Fall 7–2 to Mid Ice Crisis in November Opener
latestArticle.dek: Brave H.C. 2, Mid Ice Crisis 7 — the Braves scored twice in the third period.
paragraphs: Brave H.C. could not build on its first win of the season, falling 7–2 to Mid Ice Crisis on Sunday at Vaughan Sports Village. The Braves trailed 4–0 after two periods before Stefano Mazzei and Adam Povegliano scored in the third.

Mid Ice Crisis entered the game second in the eight-team Cristillo Division at 3–2, with 20 goals scored and 13 allowed through five games. The club had lost 2–1 to division-leading Mohawks HC the previous week. Against Mid Ice Crisis, the Braves had gone 1–2–2 in five previous regular-season meetings, including a 3–3 tie on December 14, 2025. Including two playoff losses, their record in the matchup stood at 1–4–2.

The Braves dressed 11 full-timers and two part-timers. Captain Adam Brutto, Anthony Paolucci and Keith Pearsoll were out of the lineup. Part-timer Adam Kober made his fifth appearance of the season, while part-timer Stefano Mazzei made his season debut. Marco Congiusti also made his first appearance of the season, and Brian Haspel made his Braves debut in goal.
First Period — Mid Ice Crisis Takes the Lead

Mid Ice Crisis opened the scoring at 9:14 remaining and carried a 1–0 lead into the intermission. A two-minute tripping penalty against Mid Ice Crisis at 6:51 gave the Braves a power-play opportunity, but they did not score.
Second Period — Mid Ice Crisis Builds a Four-Goal Advantage
Mid Ice Crisis scored three unanswered goals at 9:22, 1:16 and 0:35 remaining. The Braves went into the third period trailing 4–0.
Third Period — Two Different Finishes for the Braves

At 8:53 remaining, Stefano Mazzei streaked up the far side after a pass from Alex Pagnotta, then came in and beat the goaltender cleanly with a wrist shot. The goal, Mazzei's first goal of the game and first of the season in his season debut, put Brave H.C. on the scoreboard at 4–1 and gave Pagnotta his fifth assist of the season.
Mid Ice Crisis responded at 4:22 and 2:40 remaining, moving ahead 6–1.

At 1:47 remaining, Justin Carosi won the faceoff cleanly back to Alex Pagnotta. Adam Povegliano gathered the rebound and scored. The finish was Povegliano's first goal of the game and second of the season. Pagnotta received his sixth assist of the season, while Carosi picked up his second. The goal made it 6–2 before Mid Ice Crisis completed the scoring at 0:54 remaining for the 7–2 final.
Game Leaders and Recognition

Alex Pagnotta finished with two assists, his fifth and sixth of the season, giving him six points in six games. Mazzei and Povegliano recorded a goal apiece, while Justin Carosi had one assist and moved to four goals and two assists on the season. Brian Haspel took the loss, allowing seven goals in his first recorded appearance for the club.
Players of the Game: Alex Pagnotta, Adam Kober and Adam Povegliano.

Through six games, the Braves stand at 1–5, with 14 goals scored and 30 allowed. The result moved their regular-season record against Mid Ice Crisis to 1–3–2 in six meetings, with 15 goals for and 26 against. Including playoffs, the series stands at 1–5–2 across eight meetings, with 17 goals scored and 32 allowed.
Next Up — Other Way

Brave H.C. returns to Vaughan Sports Village — D Rink on Sunday, November 8 at 9:15 p.m. to face Other Way. Third in the Cristillo Division at 2–1–2 through five games, Other Way has scored 25 goals and allowed 23. It defeated Dateline Predators 8–5 on October 18 and tied Sugo Sundays 7–7 on October 25. Other Way also beat Mid Ice Crisis 4–3 earlier this season.
The Braves will look to return to the win column following Sunday's setback.

gamePreview.headline: High-Scoring Other Way Next as Braves Look to Rebound
paragraphs: Brave H.C. has seen both sides of a scoring swing over its last two games. A six-goal breakthrough against Big Bastones delivered the club's first win of the 2026–27 season, but a 7–2 loss to Mid Ice Crisis followed on November 1. Sunday's assignment brings another challenge: Other Way, which has scored 25 goals through five published league games.

Other Way is third in the eight-team Cristillo Division at 2–1–2, with 25 goals for and 23 against. Its five-goal-per-game scoring average has come in some lively contests, including an 8–5 win over Dateline Predators and a 7–7 tie with Sugo Sundays in its last two completed games. Earlier, it traded six goals apiece with Zamboner Crew.

The numbers tell only part of the story. Other Way opened its season by beating Mid Ice Crisis 4–3, but also went scoreless in a 2–0 defeat to Big Bastones. Both opponents have already figured prominently in the Braves' season. Brave H.C. beat Big Bastones 6–4 on October 25, then fell to Mid Ice Crisis the following Sunday.

Four of Other Way's five completed opponents have also faced Brave H.C. this season. Against Zamboner Crew, Other Way drew 6–6 while the Braves lost 7–1 on October 18. Against Dateline Predators, Other Way scored eight times in a victory; Brave H.C. was held off the scoresheet in a 3–0 season-opening defeat.

Those comparisons do not establish a favourite for Sunday. They do, however, underline how differently the same teams have performed from one matchup to the next, and how quickly a game can change when Other Way's attack gets rolling.
The Braves enter Sunday at 1–5, with 14 goals scored and 30 allowed in six completed HTO games. They have scored eight times in their past two outings, but have surrendered eleven.

Against Big Bastones, three first-period goals gave the Braves an early advantage before Michael Provenzano scored twice in the third. Against Mid Ice Crisis, they were down 4–0 after two periods before Stefano Mazzei, making his season debut, and Adam Povegliano found the net in the final frame.

Sunday's meeting offers the Braves another chance to turn those scoring flashes into a more complete game. Other Way has shown it can produce goals in bunches, but its early results have also left room for opponents to answer. The puck drops at 9:15 p.m. on D Rink.

archive.headline: Braves Break Through with 6–4 Win Over Big Bastones

article.headline: Braves Break Through with 6–4 Win Over Big Bastones
article.dek: Brave H.C. 6, Big Bastones 4 — a three-goal opening period and two goals from Michael Provenzano carry the Braves to their first win.
paragraphs: Brave H.C. earned its first win of the 2026–27 season on October 25, beating Big Bastones 6–4 at Vaughan Sports Village. The Braves jumped ahead 3–0 in the first period, held on after Big Bastones closed to within a goal, and finished the night with six goals, led by Michael Provenzano's two-goal performance.

Big Bastones entered the game at 2–2, with six goals scored and eight allowed through four games. Its results included a 2–0 win over Other Way and a 4–1 loss to Mohawks HC the previous week. Brave H.C. had gone 3–2–1 in six previous regular-season meetings with Big Bastones, including a 4–2 win in October 2025.

The Braves dressed 12 full-timers and one part-timer. Marco Congiusti and Anthony Paolucci were out of the lineup, while part-timer Adam Kober made his fourth appearance of the season. Stephen Logue made his second appearance of the season in goal.

The game also marked Stephane Saindon's first appearance wearing the assistant captain's A, an honour chosen by his teammates in a team vote. He celebrated with his first goal of the season, an assist and Player of the Game recognition.
First Period — Three-Goal Start

Justin Carosi opened the scoring at 8:44 remaining with his fourth goal of the season, assisted by Keith Pearsoll. Adam Povegliano made it 2–0 at 5:04 with his first of the season, from Carosi and Francesco Triumbari. Saindon added his first of the season at 2:25, assisted by Adam Brutto and Sanjay Rajkumar, to send Brave H.C. into the intermission leading 3–0.
Second Period — Big Bastones Responds
Big Bastones scored at 7:03 remaining and again with just two seconds left, reducing the Braves' lead to 3–2 entering the third.
Third Period — Provenzano Restores the Advantage

Michael Provenzano scored at 9:20 remaining with his first goal of the season, assisted by Jamie Rosenberg and Saindon. He struck again at 6:23, his second of the game and season, with Alex Pagnotta and Kober earning the assists. The four-on-four goal put Brave H.C. up 5–2 and stood as the game-winner.
Big Bastones answered at 5:39 and 3:22 to make it 5–4. With ten seconds remaining, Rosenberg sealed the win with his first goal of the season into an empty net, assisted by Triumbari.
Game Leaders and Recognition

Provenzano led the Braves with two goals and the winner. Carosi, Saindon and Rosenberg each finished with a goal and an assist, while Povegliano scored once. Triumbari had two assists, with Pearsoll, Brutto, Rajkumar, Pagnotta and Kober adding one apiece.
Logue earned the victory with four goals against. Players of the Game were Michael Provenzano, Stephane Saindon and Stephen Logue.

After five games, the Braves stood at 1–4 with 12 goals scored and 23 allowed. The result moved their regular-season record against Big Bastones to 4–2–1 in seven games, with 24 goals for and 27 against.
Correction, November 2: An earlier version omitted assists credited to Sanjay Rajkumar and Jamie Rosenberg and misstated Adam Povegliano's points. The totals above reflect the corrected game record.

article.headline: Braves Fall 7–1 to Zamboner Crew After Early Lead
article.dek: Brave H.C. 1, Zamboner Crew 7 — Keith Pearsoll puts the Braves ahead before Zamboner Crew scores seven unanswered.
paragraphs: Brave H.C. jumped ahead early against Zamboner Crew on October 18, but Zamboner Crew answered with seven straight goals to win 7–1. Keith Pearsoll gave the Braves a first-period lead before Zamboner scored twice in the opening frame, three times in the second and twice in the third.
Zamboner Crew came in at 0–1–1 after a 6–6 tie with Other Way and a 6–2 loss to Mid Ice Crisis. The Braves were looking for their first win after three defeats to open the season.

Full-timers Marco Congiusti, Anthony Paolucci, Michael Provenzano and Sanjay Rajkumar were out of the lineup. Part-timer Adam Kober made his third appearance of the season, while Krishnan Rajasooriar made his second. Dev Leong was back in goal for his second appearance of the campaign.
First Period — Pearsoll Puts Braves Ahead

Pearsoll opened the scoring at 9:17 remaining with his first goal of the season, assisted by Stephane Saindon and Alex Pagnotta. Zamboner Crew tied the game at 7:06 and moved ahead at 5:10 to take a 2–1 lead into the intermission.
Second Period — Zamboner Pulls Away
Zamboner Crew scored three more goals, at 6:39, 3:05 and 2:57 remaining, extending its lead to 5–1 heading into the third.
Third Period — Final Two Goals
Zamboner Crew added a power-play goal at 7:45 remaining and another at 3:10 to complete the 7–1 result. Leong finished with seven goals against.
Game Leaders and Recognition
Pearsoll had the Braves' lone goal, while Saindon and Pagnotta picked up assists. Players of the Game were Keith Pearsoll, Jamie Rosenberg and Stephane Saindon.
The loss left the Braves at 0–4 with six goals scored and 19 allowed.

article.headline: Braves Edged 3–2 by Michelob Morts
article.dek: Brave H.C. 2, Michelob Morts 3 — a third-period goal decides the game after a 2–2 opening period.
paragraphs: Brave H.C. lost a close 3–2 decision to Michelob Morts on October 4. Twice the Braves answered a first-period deficit, but the teams were still level at 2–2 after two periods before Michelob Morts scored the only goal of the third.

Michelob Morts entered with two wins in two games, having beaten Mohawks HC 4–3 and Dateline Predators 3–1. The meeting gave the Braves a chance to test themselves against a team that had started the season strongly.

Full-timers Marco Congiusti, Anthony Paolucci, Keith Pearsoll and Stephane Saindon were out of the lineup. Part-timers Nolan Atkins and Adam Kober made their second appearances of the season, while Damian Pavaday made his season debut. Adam Carlyle made his first appearance for the Braves in goal.
First Period — Four Goals Split Evenly

Michelob Morts struck at 9:12 remaining, but Henry Kong answered at 7:10 with his first goal of the season, assisted by Kober and Pavaday. After Michelob Morts moved ahead again at 3:36, Justin Carosi tied it just seven seconds later at 3:29, scoring his third goal of the season from Michael Provenzano.
Second Period — Deadlocked
Neither team scored in the second period, keeping the contest tied 2–2 heading into the third.
Third Period — One Goal Makes the Difference
Michelob Morts took the lead at 6:38 remaining and held on for the 3–2 win. Carlyle was charged with three goals against.
Game Leaders and Recognition
Kong and Carosi supplied the Braves' goals, with Kober, Pavaday and Provenzano recording assists. Carosi's third of the season accounted for three of the club's first five goals.
Players of the Game: Justin Carosi, Henry Kong and Adam Carlyle.
Through three games, the Braves were 0–3 with five goals scored and 12 allowed.

article.headline: Braves Fall 6–3 to Mohawks as Provenzano Reaches 50 Career Points
article.dek: Brave H.C. 3, Mohawks H.C. 6 — Justin Carosi scores twice and Michael Provenzano reaches 50 career points.
paragraphs: Brave H.C. fell 6–3 to Mohawks H.C. on September 27 despite two goals from Justin Carosi and a third-period finish by part-timer Adam Kober. The Mohawks carried a 3–1 lead into the final period and stretched their advantage to five before the Braves scored twice late.

The Mohawks arrived after a 4–3 season-opening loss to Sugo Sundays. They were familiar opponents for Brave H.C., which entered the game 16–18–8 through 42 regular-season meetings with the Mohawks, with 161 goals for and 155 against. Their previous meeting had ended 3–2 for the Mohawks in September 2025.

Full-timers Anthony Paolucci and Adam Povegliano were out of the lineup. Part-timers Nolan Atkins, Lorcan Duffy, Adam Kober and Krishnan Rajasooriar made their first appearances of the season. Stephen Logue made his first appearance of the campaign in goal.
First Period — Mohawks Strike First
The Mohawks opened the scoring with 2:42 remaining in the first period, taking a 1–0 lead into the intermission.
Second Period — Carosi Answers

Carosi tied the game 1–1 at 9:26 remaining with his first goal of the season, assisted by Michael Provenzano and Alex Pagnotta. The Mohawks responded with two goals later in the period and headed to the third leading 3–1.
Third Period — Late Braves Goals

Three more Mohawks goals made it 6–1 before Carosi scored his second goal of the game and season at 5:30 remaining, assisted again by Provenzano. Kober added his first goal of the season at 1:20, from Henry Kong and Pagnotta, to complete the scoring at 6–3.
Game Leaders and Recognition
Carosi finished with two goals, while Provenzano and Pagnotta recorded two assists apiece. Kober supplied the other Braves goal, and Logue was charged with six goals against in his first appearance.
Provenzano's two-assist game carried an additional milestone: he reached 50 career points with Brave H.C.
Players of the Game: Justin Carosi, Adam Kober and Stephen Logue.
After two games, Brave H.C. stood at 0–2 with three goals scored and nine allowed.

article.headline: Braves Open Season with 3–0 Loss to Dateline Predators
article.dek: Brave H.C. 0, Dateline Predators 3 — the opener also marks Justin Carosi’s 300th career game.
paragraphs: Brave H.C. opened the 2026–27 season with a 3–0 loss to Dateline Predators on September 20. The clubs played a scoreless first period before the Predators struck twice in the second and added another in the third.

The Predators entered the season coming off a 7–15–2 winter, when they scored 45 goals and allowed 95. The Braves, meanwhile, had won eight of their previous ten regular-season meetings against Dateline, scoring 41 goals and allowing 22. Their most recent encounter had been a 4–3 Predators win in March.

The Braves dressed 14 skaters, with full-timers Marco Congiusti and Jamie Rosenberg out of the lineup. Part-timer Stefano Ardizzi made his first appearance of the season, and Dev Leong was in goal for his season debut.
First Period — Scoreless Opening
Neither team found the net in the opening period, sending the game into the first intermission tied 0–0.
Second Period — Dateline Breaks Through
Dateline scored twice in 20 seconds, with goals at 5:11 and 4:51 remaining, to take a 2–0 lead into the third.
Third Period — Predators Finish the Job
The Predators added their final goal at 8:05 remaining to complete the 3–0 result. Leong finished with three goals against in the loss.
Milestone and Recognition
Justin Carosi reached 300 career games in the season opener. It was a major personal milestone on a difficult night for the team.
Players of the Game: Justin Carosi, Michael Provenzano and Dev Leong.
Brave H.C. ended opening night at 0–1, with no goals scored and three allowed. The result also narrowed the club's regular-season advantage over Dateline Predators to 8–3 through 11 meetings.
